messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] high OOM rate on runtime-pool-us-east-1 (auto-generated)
incident-bot: severity=high, symptom=OOM/container-restart/node-flap, nodes=3, metric=oom_count>50m

maya_oncall: ack — I'm on it. Seeing a spike in paging and CUDA OOMs in the logs for several pods in pool-us-east-1. Starting triage.

sanjay_runtime: can you paste a sample log? curious if it's typical cudaMalloc failure or something from the paged attention allocator.

maya_oncall: here's a snippet from pod runtime-frontend-7f6c:
```
2026-03-14T02:58:13Z runtime ERROR cudaMalloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
2026-03-14T02:58:13Z runtime WARN kv_cache: page_alloc failed, free_candidates=12, fragmented_bytes=1.3GB
2026-03-14T02:58:13Z runtime ERROR pager: failed to pin page -> fallback triggered
```

leo_sre: metrics show steady memory drift across the pool for ~36h. Fragmentation increases after long-lived sessions hit heavy KV churn (many distinct keys). Paging rate (pages/sec) up 4x. This looks like slow creak -> OOM pattern, not a sudden regression.

ryan_infra: I see node flaps around 03:12UTC where kernel OOM killed containerd children on 3 nodes. Suggest cordon + drain affected nodes and restart GPU drivers after a safe reboot. Also raising cluster-level pod disruption budget temporarily.

maya_oncall: starting cordon/drain for node gpu-us-east-7 and gpu-us-east-9. Also disabling autoscaler burst to avoid scheduling more pods onto strained hosts. Patch command I'm running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-us-east-7
kubectl drain gpu-us-east-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

dina_engineer: we can toggle an emergency runtime flag to aggressively compact the KV cache and reduce lifetime of very low-hit prefixes. Patch ready to flip: `runtime.kv.compact.enabled=true` + `runtime.kv.compact.threshold=0.2` (evict entries with hit < 20%). Also a quick fallback policy: route heavy sessions to quantized-medium model if OOM spike > 15%.

maya_oncall: sanjay, can you apply the compact flag? I'll do the node drains.

sanjay_runtime: applied KV compaction flags to the affected deployment and bumped `kv_compact_interval` to 30s. Also enabled `runtime.kv.forced_reclaim=true` for a short window. Restarted runtime pods on 3 nodes. Watching metrics.

maya_oncall: after restarts + compaction, paging/sec dropped ~60% on affected nodes. OOMs reduced from ~12/min to 1-2/min. Still seeing one noisy pod with repeated small OOMs — isolating it.

anya_cs: which customers were affected? any 5xxs or rate limits hitting downstream? We need a customer note asap if tenants saw errors.

maya_oncall: preliminary impact: tenant-alpha and tenant-beta had elevated 5xx for ~20 minutes during the node flaps. We throttled some requests and sent 503 for heavy sessions. Preparing a short status note.

leo_sre: long term: we should patch the allocator to perform background defragmentation of KV slabs and add telemetry for per-prefix fragmentation. Filed follow-up: INFRA-1217. Also add a burn-in job that simulates long-tail KV growth to catch this pattern in staging.

ryan_infra: scheduling a maintenance window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC to roll the pool with updated GPU drivers and kernel parameters (vm.min_free_kbytes tweak). Will reserve extra capacity and notify oncall.

sanjay_runtime: note on mitigation effectiveness: enabling compaction + restart reduced memory pressure quickly. However this is symptomatic — root cause likely allocator fragmentation + long-lived low-hit keys. We'll push a micropatch next week to add slab coalescing.

maya_oncall: handoff for next shift @dina_engineer will own follow-up until remediation is shipped. Action items in thread:
- keep `runtime.kv.compact.enabled=true` for 6h, then revert if stable
- monitor oom_count, paging/sec, evict_rate
- CS to triage impacted tenants and send notice
- SRE/Infra to complete node repro and defrag plan

anya_cs: drafting customer note: short apology, summary of what happened, impacted tenants, timeframe, and steps we're taking. Ping me in #marketing for review. :pray:

incident-bot: [UPDATE] alert status=investigating -> mitigated (partial). OOM rate decreased but follow-ups remain.

leo_sre: good catch all. Please file an incident postmortem once we have timeline + patch.

maya_oncall: handing off now — leaving notes in PagerDuty, tagging owners. Next oncall please revert the emergency flags only after 6h stable window. /me out :wave:

sanjay_runtime: ack. I'll keep a watch and post metrics snapshot in 30m.

anya_cs: thanks team. I'll send initial customer comms and escalate any high-priority requests.

maya_oncall: thanks everyone.
